result:
**Design: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE, short JWT access token, rotating device-bound refresh token, server-side session per device.**

## Sign-in
- System browser only (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`, Android Custom Tabs). No embedded webview.
- Passkeys primary. Password + TOTP fallback. Rate-limit by account and IP.
- App generates a non-exportable key pair in Secure Enclave / StrongBox at first sign-in. Server binds session to that key (DPoP).
- Server creates one `sessions` row per device: `id, user_id, family_id, refresh_hash, key_thumbprint, device_name, created_at, last_used_at, expires_at, revoked_at`.
- New-device sign-in sends email or push to user.

## Tokens
- **Access:** JWT, ES256, 10 min, claims `sub, sid, aud, exp`. Hold in memory only.
- **Refresh:** opaque 256-bit random, stored as hash on the server. 30 days idle, 90 days absolute.
- Store refresh token in iOS Keychain (`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`) or Android Keystore-encrypted storage. Never plain `SharedPreferences` / `AsyncStorage`.

## Refresh
- `POST /auth/refresh` with refresh token + DPoP proof. Returns new access token and new refresh token; old one is invalidated.
- Reuse of an old refresh token revokes the whole `family_id`. This is the token theft signal.
- Allow a 10 s grace window: the same old token inside the window returns the same new pair. Without it, flaky networks log out real users.
- Client: single-flight refresh. On 401, refresh once, retry once, else go to sign-in.

## Logout
- `POST /auth/logout`: set `revoked_at`, delete push token for that device. Client deletes Keychain item and local cache.
- `POST /auth/logout-all`: revoke every session for the user.
- The access token is still valid for up to 10 min. Close the gap with a Redis denylist of revoked `sid`, TTL 10 min, checked on every request.

## Lost phone
1. User signs in on another device or web, opens `GET /sessions`, calls `DELETE /sessions/{id}`.
2. Refresh fails at once. Access token dies at once with denylist, else within 10 min.
3. App on the lost phone gets `401 session_revoked` and wipes local data.
4. Password change or account recovery revokes all other sessions.

Limits and mitigations:
- An offline phone cannot be wiped remotely. Encrypt cached data with a Keychain-held key and cache little.
- Phone thief with unlocked phone has a live session until revoke. For sensitive apps, gate the refresh token behind biometrics (`.biometryCurrentSet`, `setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)`).
- Require fresh auth (under 5 min) for email change, password change, payouts, account delete.
- The phone may have been the only factor. Issue recovery codes at enrollment; synced passkeys cover most cases. A support-driven reset needs a delay of 24 to 72 h plus notification to all contact channels.

Lifetimes above suit a consumer app. For banking or health, cut refresh to 15 min idle / 12 h absolute and require biometric unlock on every open.
